kich_ban: There is a promise in Deuteronomy, chapter thirty-one, verse eight. Moses was old, and he was handing an entire nation over to a younger man named Joshua, and Joshua was about to walk into a land he had never set foot in.

kich_ban: And then I remember who first received this promise. Moses said it to Joshua, and what Joshua walked into next was not comfort. It was years of war. Campaign after campaign. Losses. A whole generation of hard mornings. The promise was never that the road would be easy. The promise was that Joshua would not walk it first, and would not walk it alone.

kich_ban: In Habakkuk, chapter two, verse three, the prophet is told that what God has spoken has an appointed time, and that it will not lie. I am not going to use that verse to tell you what you owe me.

y_chinh: God's timing is deliberate and never disorganized

kich_ban: I am going to use it to say something about you. You keep appointments I cannot see on a calendar nobody has shown me. You are never disorganized, and never too busy with the size of the world to keep a date you set for me. You are deliberate, and you are kind, and those two things have never been in conflict in you.

y_chinh: Waiting becomes watchful rather than bitter

kich_ban: Habakkuk went up on the watchtower to wait and to keep looking. He did not stop asking hard questions. He simply asked them from a higher place. So put me on that tower this morning. Let me wait without becoming bitter. Let me ask without accusing you. Let me keep watching for you in the hours ahead. You have not forgotten what I asked you for.

kich_ban: Right now, while I am sitting here, someone is already in the hardest part of their day. Somewhere a person is driving to an appointment they have not told anyone about. They will hear a result today, and they made that drive alone on purpose. Go before them into that room. Guide the doctors and nurses who care for them. Bless the medicine and the treatments.

kich_ban: You are going ahead of every one of them, by name, at the same time, without ever dividing your attention. Go before every window that lit up this morning. And now the ones nobody is praying for.

kich_ban: There is a person who lives alone, and today not one voice will say their name out loud. Not at a table. Not on a phone. They will speak to a cashier and that will be the conversation of their day. Say their name, Father. Let them be certain, somehow, that they were thought of before the sun came up.

They just cannot walk back through that door yet, and they have stopped telling anyone that they pray. Go before them. Do not send them a lecture. Send them someone safe. Remind them that you never left when the people did.

kich_ban: And there is a person who will be treated unfairly at work before this day is over. They will be spoken to in a way no one should be spoken to, and they will need the job too much to answer back. Stand beside them. Guard their dignity when they cannot defend it.

kich_ban: You know each of them the way you know me. Not as a category. Not as a crowd. As a name you have said before, in a house you have already walked through. Say their names, since no one else will today.

kich_ban: Jesus said that not one sparrow falls to the ground outside the Father's care. He said the hairs of your head are numbered. And he said that to people who were about to be handed over, arrested, dragged in front of officials for his name. He did not say the sparrow never falls. He said the sparrow never falls unnoticed.

kich_ban: That is a harder comfort and a better one. He was not promising them a life where nothing breaks. He was telling them that nothing about them was too small to be counted, even in the worst week of their lives.

y_chinh: God notices details no one else counts

kich_ban: So here is what settles me this morning. If you are counting sparrows, you are counting the parts of today that no one else will ever notice.

kich_ban: The tiredness behind my eyes that I will not mention to anyone. The three minutes I will spend in the car before I go inside, gathering myself. The thing I will do well today that nobody will thank me for. The kind sentence I will say that nobody will repeat. None of that falls outside your attention.

kich_ban: Earlier I thanked you for the hours I cannot remember. This is the same mercy in daylight. What you did in the dark while I slept, you are doing in the details while I am awake. You have never handed me off to anyone. You have never lost track of a single day I have lived. You have never once been careless with my life.

kich_ban: So I am deciding something before my feet touch the floor. I choose to believe that this day already has your footprints on it. I will not spend this morning rehearsing conversations that may never happen. I will not treat my own worry as if it were preparation.

kich_ban: I trust you with the hour I am most afraid of. I trust you with the answer I have not received. I trust you with the part of today I have not even imagined yet.

kich_ban: And I will move. I will do the next thing in front of me. I will make the call, open the message, have the conversation, and take the step, knowing that I am not the one breaking the ground.

kich_ban: And I am going to start with the one I have been avoiding longest. Not because I feel brave this morning, because I do not. But because standing still has cost me more than any of these things ever have, and because whatever is on the other side of that door, you are already in the room.

kich_ban: If today goes the way I hope, I will remember who went first. And if it does not, I will still be walking behind the same God, and I will not go looking for another shelter. I am not the first one walking into today.

y_chinh: Scripture repeats the promise at the threshold of action

kich_ban: So listen to this before you stand up. Deuteronomy, chapter thirty-one, verse eight. He goes before you. He is with you. He will not fail you and he will not abandon you. That was not written for the easy season of a man's life. It was written for the morning he stepped into something he had never done before.

y_chinh: The opening worries are gathered under one faithful perspective

kich_ban: You woke up tired of a day that had not happened yet. Someone has already walked into it. The conversation. The news you are waiting on. The person you have to face. The work still leaning on this morning. All four have now been prayed over by name. His going ahead of you never meant the road would be easy.

y_chinh: The listener sees evidence of a way already prepared

kich_ban: It means you are not first, and you are not alone. You can choose that now, standing right here, before you have any proof. Look down at the road in front of you. The prints are already there. You are following, not leading. Breathe once. Nothing has to be figured out in the next minute.

kich_ban: May the God who goes before you keep every hour you have not walked into yet. May he speak your name in the rooms where you are not standing. May he move what is standing in your road before you reach it. And if he has not moved it yet, may you know that he is standing right there with you.

kich_ban: Everything you have asked this morning, leave it in hands that were here before you woke up. In the name of Jesus. Amen. If you agree with that, type one word in the comments. Ahead. Just that. Then send this to someone you know is walking into something hard before tonight. It may be the only prayer said over them today.

kich_ban: And if this is how you want to meet him tomorrow, we will be here at this same hour. A like helps someone else find this in the dark.

kich_ban: We prayed the hard question this morning. There is one more, and it does not belong to dawn. It belongs to the hour when this quiet starts to thin and the day asks you to prove you meant it. That prayer is waiting for you right here.
